title: Deconfounding Game 1: smoking and miscarriage
content: Smoking acts through an unobserved underlying abnormality that can cause both prior and future miscarriage. Prior miscarriage is therefore a descendant and proxy for part of the causal mechanism, not a confounder to adjust away.

variables.name: Smoking (X)
variables.content: The proposed cause whose total effect on future miscarriage is sought.

variables.name: Underlying Abnormality (A)
variables.content: An unobservable abnormality induced by smoking and capable of causing miscarriage.

variables.name: Future Miscarriage (Y)
variables.content: The outcome whose causal response to smoking is being estimated.

variables.name: Prior Miscarriage (B)
variables.content: Observed miscarriage history caused by the same underlying abnormality.

arrows.because: The source defines A as an underlying abnormality induced by smoking.
The abnormality is the mechanism through which smoking can cause a future miscarriage.
Prior miscarriage history is another consequence of the same abnormality.
